---
title: "LargeST: reproduce the two regional flow maps"
output: html_document
params:
  snapshot: "../../data/LargeST Data/processed/largest-visualization.json.gz"
---

This tutorial reproduces the Los Angeles and Bay Area **data layers** in the
repository's LargeST visualization for July 31, 2019. The standalone dataset, extracted losslessly from the HTML, contains actual
saved sensor and display-link series for 288 five-minute frames. No original
HDF5 download, synthetic replacement, fitting or browser execution is needed.

## Read the standalone visualization dataset

Install `bdynets` and `jsonlite`; rendering also requires `rmarkdown` and `knitr`.
The reader loads standalone JSON and records its MD5 and original HTML SHA-256.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(bdynets)
snapshot <- read_traffic_data(params$snapshot)
snapshot$provenance
lapply(snapshot$data$regions, function(region) region$summary)
```

Sensor observations and display links are separate. The original visualization
constructed links between selected sensors and assigned endpoint-averaged flow
values. The importer retains those saved links and rounded values; it does not
promote them to physical connectivity or model adjacency. Null values remain
missing and use the original gray color.

## Reproduce the original default time

The original viewer opens at 16:10, JavaScript index 194. The corresponding
one-based R index is 195. Both regions use their own saved quantile thresholds,
so identical colors do **not** imply identical flow across regions.

```{r reproduce, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
frames <- traffic_figures(params$snapshot, "largest", time_index=195L)
```

The maps retain the source seven-color scale, geographic link geometry and
opposite-direction offsets at each region's source zoom. Flow values are those
saved in the viewer. Geometry is projected to Web Mercator. Remote basemap tiles,
place labels and browser controls are omitted; static line widths are adapted
to the graphics device. These are data-layer reproductions, not pixel-identical
screenshots or a reconstruction of the full road network.

## Choose a region, time and export destination

```{r options, eval=FALSE}
frame <- traffic_frame(snapshot, time_index=97L, region="Bay Area")
plot(frame) # 08:00
traffic_figures(params$snapshot, "largest", time_index=97L,
                output_dir="/path/to/new/largest-0800")
```

The export writes both regional maps as PDF/PNG, source identity, frame selection
and session information. It refuses existing named outputs. For statistical
analysis, use the sensor-level series and documented graph construction rather
than treating display-link averages as independent count observations.

```{r thresholds}
lapply(snapshot$data$regions, function(region) unlist(region$breaks))
sessionInfo()
```
